notes: This is the second REVISE on the final review. Per the rubric: 'Two consecutive REVISE on final → ABORT.' The prior round-2 review already issued REVISE with five specific findings; this round-3 evidence resolves some (table now lists Phases 8/9, tool count math reconciled, rc1 tag claim refined) but the two load-bearing failures remain: Phase 8 streaming is still entirely absent (FAIL on dimension 2 per rubric's explicit 'real, not stubbed' requirement), and golden goals were still never executed end-to-end (FAIL on dimension 1, with no attempt to run even the sandbox-only 'build' goal despite the Phase 7 live demo proving the executor works against vLLM). Evidence honesty is intact — gaps are disclosed plainly — so the ABORT is structural (rubric mapping), not a credibility failure. The sprint produced substantial value (7 phases approved, 229 tests, ReAct executor proven via live demo) but does not meet the v0.5.0 bar.
findings: Per rubric verdict mapping, two consecutive REVISE on final → ABORT. This is that ABORT. The path forward is not another revise round on this sprint; it is to decide with Joshua whether to (a) open a short v0.5.1 sprint to add minimal streaming + run golden goals, or (b) formally amend the rubric to cut streaming from v0.5 scope and re-grade.

Dimension 2 FAIL persists: no streaming implementation exists. diff_stat shows no streaming module added in this final phase. Rubric requires P1 streaming to be 'real, not behind a future work flag.' The deferral is honestly disclosed but does not satisfy the criterion.

Dimension 1 FAIL persists: golden goals not executed. The round-2 review explicitly suggested running at minimum the sandbox-only 'build' goal to convert this to PARTIAL. The round-3 evidence does not show this was attempted. The Phase 7 live demo (fibonacci(50)) is functionally close to the 'build' goal and proves the executor works, but it is not the golden goal harness output.

tests/golden_goals.yaml does not exist (disclosed in evidence). The golden goal runner is therefore untested infrastructure. If a v0.5.1 sprint is opened, creating this YAML and running at least one goal end-to-end is the smallest unblocking action.

For the next sprint or rubric amendment: the 'crawl4ai broken (lxml 6.0.2 vs 5.3)' blocker is a one-line pyproject.toml constraint (lxml<6) plus a rebuild. The SearXNG 404 is likely a wrong endpoint path (/search vs /). Both are <1h fixes and should not be carried as gaps into a release.
